projectBackground.name: Meridian Credit Facility Review
projectBackground.context: Meridian wants a term loan secured on a warehouse. Cash flow has been volatile and a covenant breach is possible.

manager.name: Jonas Brandt
manager.note: The committee wants one clear recommendation and the three numbers that justify it. Tell me what could go wrong, not only what looks good.

assignment.title: Recommend whether and how to lend
assignment.brief: Compute coverage and collateral ratios, rank three borrowers in Excel and write a short credit recommendation with conditions.

tasks.title: Debt Service Coverage Ratio
tasks.prompt: EBITDA is €1,440,000 and annual debt service is €1,200,000. What is the DSCR?
tasks.reasoning: DSCR shows how many times operating cash covers debt payments; below 1.0 means debt cannot be serviced.
tasks.tip: Define DSCR consistently with the covenant definition.
tasks.mistake: Using net profit instead of EBITDA changes the ratio materially.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Loan-to-Value
tasks.prompt: The loan is €700,000 against collateral valued at €1,000,000. What is the LTV percentage?
tasks.reasoning: LTV measures how much of the collateral value is lent; higher LTV means less cushion.
tasks.tip: Ask what haircut applies in a forced sale.
tasks.mistake: Ignoring forced-sale value overstates the security.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Credit Assessment Framework
tasks.prompt: Which set is the classic framework for assessing a borrower?
options: Character, capacity, capital, collateral and conditions
Cost, cash, culture, clients and competition
Revenue, margin, growth, tax and dividends
Brand, price, product, place and promotion
tasks.reasoning: The five Cs cover willingness to pay, ability to repay, equity cushion, security and the environment.
tasks.tip: Use all five, not just collateral.
tasks.mistake: Relying on collateral alone ignores whether the borrower can actually repay.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Covenant Design
tasks.prompt: Select sensible financial covenants for this facility.
options: Requirement to use a named supplier
tasks.reasoning: Financial covenants should be measurable, tied to repayment capacity and monitored regularly.
tasks.tip: A covenant you cannot measure is not a covenant.
tasks.mistake: Non-financial restrictions unrelated to risk create friction without protection.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Borrower Ranking (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Calculate Debt/EBITDA (E = C / B) and DSCR (F = B / D) for the three borrowers and upload.
tasks.reasoning: Ranking borrowers on both leverage and coverage shows who can carry more debt and who is already stretched.
tasks.tip: Beta's DSCR below 1.0 is a decline signal.
tasks.mistake: Looking only at leverage misses cash-flow stress.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Credit Recommendation
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence credit recommendation for Meridian (DSCR 1.20x, LTV 70%).
tasks.modelAnswer: I recommend approval subject to conditions. Meridian's DSCR of 1.20x covers debt service but leaves limited headroom, and the 70% LTV is acceptable provided the warehouse valuation is independently confirmed. I propose a quarterly minimum DSCR covenant of 1.15x, delivery of monthly management accounts and a cash sweep if DSCR falls below 1.10x. The key risk is volatile cash flow, so a debt service reserve account equal to three months is advised. If the covenants are not agreed, I would reduce the facility size.
tasks.reasoning: A credit memo recommends a decision, cites the key ratios, identifies the main risk and proposes mitigants.
tasks.mistake: Presenting ratios without a decision leaves the committee to guess.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Covenant Nobody Monitored
caseStudy.background: A lender approved a facility with a DSCR covenant but never tracked it. The borrower breached for three quarters before anyone noticed, and recovery cost was far higher than early intervention would have been.
caseStudy.challenges: Covenant compliance reports were not received or reviewed.
caseStudy.constraints: No owner was assigned to monitoring.
questions: Why is a covenant useless without monitoring?
What process would have flagged the breach?
caseStudy.solution: Quantis introduced a quarterly covenant dashboard with automatic escalation after a missed submission.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Credit risk is managed after approval too; monitor, escalate and document.
